questions.q: State the difference between a variable and a constant.

markPoints.concept: a variable's value can change while the program runs; a constant's cannot
markPoints.exemplar: A variable's value can change while the program runs; a constant's cannot.

questions.example: A variable can hold a different value at different points while the program runs, whereas a constant keeps the same value throughout.
questions.paraphrase: The value held in a variable may be altered as the program executes, while a constant stays fixed.
questions.feedback: Both halves. Saying only 'a constant never changes' leaves out what a variable does.
questions.revisitLabel: 2.2 Lesson 1 — Variable store, station 1: Variables and assignment

questions.q: Why would a programmer use a constant for the rate of VAT rather than typing the number in several places?
options: If the rate changes, only one line has to be edited
Constants are processed faster than numbers
A constant uses less memory than a number
Numbers cannot be used in calculations directly
questions.feedback: One place to change, and no risk of missing one of them.
questions.revisitLabel: 2.2 Lesson 1 — Variable store, station 1: Variables and assignment

questions.q: Match each programming construct to what it does to the order a program runs in.
pairs: Each line is carried out one after the other
A choice is made, and only one route is taken
A block of code is repeated
questions.feedback: Sequence, selection, iteration — every program is built from these three.
